$meta.name: LongClaw design tokens
$meta.contract: Both axes are independent. Apply data-appearance and data-theme on the same root element (<html>). Components consume only --lc-* tokens; no component may hardcode an accent hue. Switching theme or appearance is a token swap and nothing else.
$meta.notes: Color values that differ from the approved visual reference were adjusted to clear WCAG AA; every adjustment is recorded in ../decisions.md and verified by ../scripts/a11y-check.mjs.

z.note: Every layer the app stacks, lowest first. A positioned element with any z-index outranks one with z-index: auto, so a surface meant to be on top that says nothing loses to a sticky list header that says 1 — which is how the open ticket panel came to be painted over by the list behind it (LC-96). The scale is the whole set: a positioned surface takes a layer from it rather than a number of its own. drag is the drop indicator a drag draws over the rows: it is rendered before them, so at auto every row painted over it and the list's — which straddles a row boundary — lost a pixel of itself to any row wearing a background (LC-154). It sits below sticky because a group header stays on top of what scrolls under it, indicator included. popover sits above modal because quick create carries the status, priority and label menus, and a menu behind its own modal is unusable. The workspace is the floor and deliberately has no layer: giving one to an ancestor of the board and list would make it a stacking context, and the menu popover renders inline rather than through a portal, so a menu opened from a card would be trapped under the panel. For the same reason these numbers order the surfaces that stack at the root; a popover rendered inside the panel is ordered within it and bounded by the panel's own layer. The board's and list's rows take no layer of their own: they are placed by geometry that never overlaps them, and a stacking context per row is a cost the scroller pays 5,000 times for a relation it does not have. scripts/stacking-guard.mjs holds the relations.

motion.note: Motion communicates state, never decorates. The agent pulse (900ms ease-out, two beats) is the one exception to the sub-150ms rule: it is the designed acknowledgement of an external file edit. `spinner` is the delayed write indicator's rotation — the same period as the pulse but a separate token, because reusing the pulse's would tie a loading spin to the agent's acknowledgement and neither could then be retuned alone.

elevation.note: Dark surfaces carry elevation with the raised color and hairlines, not shadow. Cards in dark have no shadow.

mix.note: Percentages for color-mix(in oklab, accent N%, base) derivations, per appearance. These make every soft/tint variant a pure derivation of the two accent tokens, so a theme preset only supplies accents.

raised.role: hover surfaces, popovers; light pairs with elevation.overlay

wash.role: code surfaces — inline chips and fenced blocks alike (LC-97, LC-98) — quiet fills, progress track

raised-hover.role: hover fill for anything already sitting on `raised` — secondary buttons and popover rows. In dark, `raised` and `wash` are the same value, so a control resting on `raised` that hovered to `wash` gave no feedback at all; this is the step components.md:52 calls the raised hover overlay.

ink-3.role: meta, timestamps, placeholders — AA-adjusted from reference #878CA0/#676C80

tile.role: agent avatar tile — a terminal window in miniature; always near-black in both appearances, so anything painted on it must name a light ink rather than inherit one (scripts/tile-contrast-guard.mjs)

status.note: Status = color dot + text label (founder revision 2026-07-28, decisions.md D3 — retires the reference's pie/check/X glyphs). One dot geometry: the default state is an unfilled ring (today's Todo); every other state is the same dot filled with the status color. Statuses are user-definable: a new status always gets a color, defaulting to the grey ring; user choices come from the label ramp. The dot never appears without its label except on the board, where the column header names it. Done still routes to the human accent (D5) and green is never offered. Theme-independent except done. AA: built-in dot colors ≥ 3:1 against surface and bg; user-ramp dots lean on the mandatory label, like label chips.

backlog.glyph: dashed ring — before the default state; the dash survives every CVD type

todo.glyph: open ring — THE default state and the default for new statuses

in-progress.glyph: filled dot — AA-adjusted from reference #DE9B0D in light

in-review.glyph: filled dot — AA-adjusted from reference #E5732A in light

done.glyph: filled dot in the human accent

priority.note: Six levels: Urgent · P1 · P2 · P3 · P4 · None (founder revision 2026-07-28, decisions.md D4 — replaces the reference's High/Medium/Low bar glyphs). P1–P4 are bordered mono chips, monochrome except urgent; the number carries the level. Chip text is real text, held to 4.5:1; the border is a decorative container.

warn.role: conflicts, unreachable folder — AA-adjusted from reference #B45309 in light

warn-ink.role: secondary action text inside warn banners

danger.role: destructive actions, parse errors — AA-adjusted from reference #D64545 in light

label.note: Fixed system ramp for project labels; never themed. Dots are reinforcement only — the chip text is the identifier — so dots are not held to 3:1. The green band (hue 120–165) is excluded: green belongs to the agent, exclusively.

alias.note: A role that is a *decision about* another token rather than a hue of its own. It emits `--lc-<name>: var(--lc-<of>)`, so the decision is made once, here, and the components that consume it say what they are rather than which neutral they happen to sit on. `of` must name a color.neutral key; build.mjs fails on one that does not.

code-surface.role: inline code chips and fenced blocks (LC-97, LC-98). Was `tile` — the agent's terminal window, near-black in *both* appearances — so the inherited ink painted itself and every backtick rendered as a black rectangle. `wash` flips with the appearance, which is the property the decision turns on. Note that `wash` and `raised` share a value in dark, so code rendered *on* a raised surface would need this to move rather than the rules that consume it.

code-ink.role: the ink that pairs with `code-surface`. Named rather than inherited so a blockquote's dimmed `ink-2` cannot follow code into a chip; a link's accent still wins, because a link is an affordance rather than a surface.

themes.note: A theme preset supplies exactly four accent decisions per appearance: the accent (fills, rings, borders), the text variant (AA ≥ 4.5:1 as small text on surface and soft chips), the on-accent color (button labels, glyph marks on accent fills), and nothing else. Every soft/hover/ring/rail variant derives from these via mix.*. The agent pair is identical in every preset — agent activity must read the same in every project.
